Article Title: Govt distances itself from Hasina event but Dhaka not convinced
Article Text:
India has firmly denied any role in Sheikh Hasina's forthcoming media address, while Dhaka expresses skepticism, worried that the address may jeopardize diplomatic ties. Meanwhile, Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has received an invitation to the Brics summit from India, but he may encounter domestic backlash concerning the extradition of Hasina. To date, Bangladesh has not officially responded to the Brics invitation.

Ahead of former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina 's media address, the Indian government sought to distance itself from the event saying that India doesn't endorse the views that may be expressed at the event. However, Dhaka, which had raised the issue with Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi on Monday, remains unconvinced as diplomatic sources said allowing Hasina to make a political speech might rock an already unsteady relationship.Hasina, who has announced she plans to return to Bangladesh in December despite the death sentence awarded to her, is scheduled to virtually address a media event at the foreign correspondents' club on Wednesday evening. This would be Hasina's first media address since she fled to India after being deposed on August 5, 2024.The MEA said that the interaction was being organized by a private media entity. “The government has no involvement whatsoever in it. Neither does it endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum,” said spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal. The ministry recently told a Parliamentary committee that while providing refuge to Hasina, India had strictly adhered to the principle that no political activity is directed against any other country from Indian soil.The Indian government also for the first time confirmed that Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman had been invited by India for the BRICS summit that it will host in September. While PM Narendra Modi had earlier invited Rahman to India for a bilateral visit, the government said that the invitation on this occasion is for a BRICS outreach session and in Rahman's capacity as the current chair of BIMSTEC.While Bangladesh aspires for BRICS membership and has already received support from Russia and China for its candidature, Rahman will likely be wary of any domestic fallout of travelling to India amid the unresolved Hasina extradition issue. Jamaat-e-Islami's ascendancy as the primary opposition party may also restrict Rahman from soft-pedalling the Hasina issue. Dhaka has not yet formally accepted or declined the invitation that was extended by Modi to Rahman for BRICS.“You would be aware that a formal invitation for a bilateral visit to India was extended to the Bangladesh PM upon his assumption of office in Feb 2026. As far as the BRICS Summit is concerned, India has separately extended an invitation to Bangladesh PM in his capacity as the current Chair of BIMSTEC to attend the outreach session of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi,” said the spokesperson.“The invitation has been extended as per the standard practice being followed in BRICS for the outreach sessions. Other heads of regional groups have also been invited in a similar manner,” he added.
Article Summary: India has firmly denied any role in Sheikh Hasina's forthcoming media address. Dhaka expresses skepticism, worried that the address may jeopardize diplomatic ties. Meanwhile, Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has received an invitation to the Brics summit from India.

Article Title: Govt dismisses reports of fuel quality issues, says checks on
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Dismissing reports of fuel quality issues at outlets, govt Tuesday said additional checks have been introduced by oil marketing companies (OMCs) to detect fuel contamination and adulteration.In a post on X, the petroleum ministry said OMCs were regularly monitoring fuel quality, water ingress and contamination, and that only two cases of chloride contamination had been detected so far."In addition to the advanced and elaborate testing protocols already in place, further checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing 8-12 times a day at over 87,000 outlets. Over 2,000 samples have also been tested for chloride/sulphide. Only two cases of chloride contamination have been found in the entire country till now, and sales from those pumps were suspended immediately," ministry said.It added that oil companies had been instructed to take proactive steps to detect any possible contamination across the fuel supply chain, and strict action would be taken if contamination or adulteration was found at any retail outlet.Through a series of infographics on X, ministry said there was "zero compromise" on quality benchmarks and that 302 tankers carrying 10,500 kilolitres of ethanol were rejected between July 2024 and June 2026 for failing quality standards.It added that ethanol used for blending must comply with BIS IS 15464, have a minimum purity of 99.6% and be accompanied by a certified quality report. The ministry said ethanol is stored in dedicated facilities to prevent contamination, its quality is monitored regularly to ensure consistency and every tanker is sampled from both the top and bottom before being accepted.Separately, govt has so far approved Rs 4,687 crore as interest subsidy for eligible ethanol projects under its various support schemes, minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi told Parliament Monday. Under the schemes, govt bears an interest subvention of 6% or 50% of the interest rate charged by lenders, whichever is lower, for five years on loans taken to set up new distilleries or expand existing ethanol production capacity.
Article Summary: Govt: OMCs regularly monitoring fuel quality, water ingress and contamination. Only two cases of chloride contamination had been detected so far. 302 tankers carrying 10,500 kilolitres of ethanol were rejected between July 2024 and June 2026.

Article Title: 'Contamination' in fuel, says SIAM, later retracts
Article Text:
SIAM says corrosion of vehicle parts due to high chloride presence in fuel

NEW DELHI: Auto industry body SIAM flagged concerns over "high chloride" presence and moisture content in fuel resulting in a "huge increase" in issues related to vehicle parts and replacements, including fuel pumps, fuel injectors and EGR valve. It demanded stringent checks, arguing that contamination raises a wrong impression about E20 fuel in customers' minds, report Dipak Dash & Aabhas Sharma.Late evening, SIAM said it has since "withdrawn" the letter sent to petroleum ministry on July 28 that had raised these concerns, which were based on investigations of failure of vehicle parts.Some numbers quoted in the communication need authentication through collection of elaborate data from various regions across the country followed by a comprehensive consultation with our member OEMs. MoPNG has also instituted 3ppm guidelines for chloride/sulphur as a precautionary measure for all ethanol being blended into petrol supply chain, SIAM clarified late Tuesday.“All of these steps fully meet the needs of the automobile industry. Further, we understand from OMCs that checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing about 8-12 times a day in over 87,000 outlets,” it added. In the letter sent to ministry, SIAM had said investigations of failure of vehicle parts revealed that these were due to “corrosion or wear caused by high chloride presence traced to the fuel used”.It had urged the govt to “include chloride parameter” in E20 fuel specifications and its control by oil marketing companies and retail fuel outlets.SIAM said chloride was highly detrimental to engine parts as its presence or accumulation in the fuel system can lead to corrosion, which can further result in “permanent damage” to engine parts immediately or over time. “Hence, it is imperative to include the chloride limits in fuel specifications and implement quality control to avoid chloride related failures in the customer vehicles,” the letter had noted.
Article Summary: Auto industry body SIAM flagged concerns over "high chloride" presence and moisture content in fuel. It demanded stringent checks, arguing that contamination raises a wrong impression about E20 fuel in customers' minds. SIAM said it has since "withdrawn" the letter sent to petroleum ministry on July 28 that had raised these concerns.

NEW DELHI: Paving the way for expediting a new railway line to boost connectivity to the border area near the India-China-Bhutan tri-junction, West Bengal govt has given its go ahead for fast-tracking acquisition of around 380 hectares of land. With this, work on the 20-km Chalsa-Naxak new line project that was originally sanctioned in 2011-12 is likely to get speeded up.TOI has learnt that the new section, a vital component of the New Jalpaiguri-Siliguri-New Bongaigaon gauge conversion project was placed in abeyance in Sept 2019 due to non-cooperation from the earlier Trinamool govt in the state. Official records show that railways "de-freezed" (revived) the project in Jan along with five others after a six year hiatus but again failed to make any progress with the lack of support from the state govt's side.They added that soon after BJP formed govt all projects pending for years are being expedited. "Soon after Suvendu Adhikari took charge, railway minister Ashwini Vashnaw visited the state where all pending projects were reviewed and state govt has given the go ahead, including for this strategically important project," Siliguri MP Raju Bista told TOI.Earlier in the day, in a social media post, Bista said, "Happy to share that the ministry of railways has sanctioned around Rs 272 crore for a new 17-km line to Jaldhaka.The route originates from Khunia More near Chalsa, and passes through Jalpaiguri and Kalimpong forest divisions." He added that the rail link will improve connectivity to the India-China-Bhuta trijunction and boost tourism in the Jhaldhaka-Bindu-Todey Tangta area.Bista said, "The railways and Bengal forest department will carry out a joint survey after the monsoon for the proposed new line." It will connect Jaldhaka region, on the border of the river originating from a place close to Doklam tri-junction of India, Bhutan, China.
Article Summary: West Bengal govt has given its go ahead for fast-tracking acquisition of around 380 hectares of land. Work on the 20-km Chalsa-Naxak new line project that was originally sanctioned in 2011-12 is likely to get speeded up. Article Title: In MP village, kids risk lives every day, hop over dam pillars to reach school
Article Text:
Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the current education system in rural areas, like Kakraua, sufficient to support students? Yes, it meets their needs. No, it needs significant improvement. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: Children from Kakraua village in MP's Vidisha district are forced to risk their lives every day by negotiating a precarious line of concrete pillars across a check dam on the Betwa river to reach their school - a route they take to avoid a much longer commute.A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media, raising fresh concerns about local infrastructure and student safety.Kakraua has a school only up to eighth grade.The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road. By crossing the check dam, the distance shrinks to roughly 1.5km, prompting nine students - five of them girls in the ninth grade - to use the risky shortcut daily.The village is part of the constituency of former CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who is now the Union minister for agriculture.The dam-crossing involves walking across a series of exposed pillars that stand about three to four feet apart.Students hop about 10 pillars each trip. Villagers say the gap between pillars makes the route hazardous, especially during the monsoon when surfaces become slippery and the river's current increases."We have to work in the fields, so we can't drop our children off at school and back," said a parent."They find it easier to cross the dam nearby... We only have two options: we either stop sending our children to school or continue sending them this way even though it's dangerous."The consequences of skipping the unsafe route are already visible in the community.A student failed her final exams earlier this year after missing school because she could not cross the pillars due to her short height; she is repeating ninth grade this year.Parents fear that continued reliance on the shortcut could lead to further academic setbacks or, worse, an accident.District education officer N K Ahirwar acknowledged the problem. "I visited the spot and informed the collector about this," Ahirwar said."I have written to higher authorities to find a solution soon." However, he did not provide a timeline for the construction of a safe passage for river crossing.Local residents are now pressing authorities for an urgent solution to ensure uninterrupted schooling without endangering children's lives.
Article Summary: Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river to reach their school. A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media. The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road.

NEW DELHI: Govt is likely to allow a levy of 0.25% to 0.4% as merchant discount rate (MDR) or charges on UPI payments above Rs 2,000 made to businesses, while keeping payments made by one person to another outside the ambit.The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, moved by FM Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday, has sought to remove the bar on banks and payment service providers to levy MDR on notified electronic payment modes. Govt officials said there is no decision on when the proposal will be implemented.Official estimates show that the Rs 2,000 floor will cover 5% of all UPI transactions, but those transactions account for 65% of the total transaction value, and is unlikely to impact daily purchases such as milk, vegetables and groceries or even payments for auto or taxi use. In July, there were 23.7 billion transactions, whose combined value was pegged at Rs 29.9 lakh crore."Even if implemented, 95% of the transactions will not face the merchant discount rate. Besides, not all businesses are going to pass on the fees, which will be a small amount," an official said.Industry persons said govt may likely impose a ceiling on the absolute amount that is charged. "Unlike credit cards, there is no funding cost involved so it makes sense to have a ceiling once the costs are covered," said an industry source.At present, credit and debit cards come with MDR, but most merchants do not pass it on to consumers. In the case of credit card MDR, where the fee is not regulated, it can be as high as 3% of the transaction value. For debit card transactions up to Rs 20 lakh, there is a cap of 0.4%, and for higher value it is 0.9%.
Article Summary: The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, moved by FM Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday, has sought to remove the bar on banks and payment service providers to levy MDR on notified electronic payment modes. Govt officials said there is no decision on when the proposal will be implemented.

Article Title: 56% of vehicles not insured, SC says challan them
Article Text:
SC has raised alarm on the uninsured vehicles operating on road

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: If your vehicle is not insured, you may not be able to get fuel from petrol pumps in the near future. Supreme Court Tuesday suggested this as one of the measures to tackle the problem of uninsured vehicles plying on roads and also directed that cameras deployed on highways and roads be used to identify such vehicles and send challans to owners.Expressing shock that nearly 56% of vehicles plying on Indian roads remain uninsured (most of them two-wheelers), a bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Prashant Kumar Mishra said the purpose behind mandatory insurance under Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act gets defeated, resulting in victims of road accidents being forced into prolonged litigation to get compensation. In absolute terms, the stark figure of uninsured vehicles stands at 16.5 crore vehicles out of a total of 30.4 crore registered vehicles. As per govt data, 22% of road accidents involve uninsured vehicles.As per the MV Act, those who drive or allow an uninsured vehicle to be driven without valid motor third-party insurance are liable to be punished, including imprisonment, for violation of the law. In the case of a first offence, the punishment is imprisonment for up to three months, or a fine of Rs 2,000 or both; and for a subsequent offence, imprisonment for up to three months, or a fine of Rs 4,000 or both are provided."The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority, in consultation with the road transport ministry, to deliberate and evolve a pilot project whereby fuel for vehicles to be linked with valid insurance status. In the absence thereof, the vehicle concerned would be refused fuel at petrol pumps until such time valid insurance is obtained. The benefit therein is two-fold - first, it will assist in identification of uninsured or unregistered vehicles. Secondly, it will prompt the owners of these vehicles to ensure that they have valid insurance status. Such projects would ensure ground-level compliance with the statutory mandate of Section 146 of the MVA. This may be done through the use of cameras. The ministry of petroleum and natural gas, has in principle, no objection to the same," the bench said.The bench said that there should be strict implementation of law and directed that state traffic police should be given handheld devices or downloadable apps, linked with the data from Insurance Information Bureau and VAHAN portal to verify insurance status on the ground. "ANPR cameras deployed on highways and roads are equipped with a mechanism to catch and penalise road safety violations such as high speed, red light jumping, driving on the wrong side of the road, etc. Carrying this forward and as already deployed by the MoRTH in certain states, ANPR cameras are to be integrated with data from the Insurance Information Bureau and the VAHAN portal for issuance of automatic e-challans to uninsured vehicles," the bench said.The result of vehicles remaining uninsured is that accident victims and their families have no recourse to adequate compensation within a reasonable time period.In 2018, the apex court had directed mandatory buying of third-party insurance for three years for new cars and five years for two-wheelers at the time of buy/registration of new vehicles. Noting that a large number of vehicles remain uninsured, the bench increased the period by one year and directed that henceforth, a buyer has to buy third-party insurance for four years for new cars and six years for new two-wheelers.
Article Summary: Nearly 56% of vehicles plying on Indian roads remain uninsured (most of them two-wheelers) 16.5 crore vehicles out of a total of 30.4 crore registered vehicles. 22% of road accidents involve uninsured vehicles. Those who drive or allow uninsured vehicle to be driven without valid motor third-party insurance are liable to be punished.

Article Title: US Congressman warns FCRA Bill could affect India-US ties
Article Text:

A US lawmaker on Tuesday criticised the amendments proposed to India's foreign funding law, alleging that they could allow the government to take over churches and religious charities and warning that the issue could affect India-US ties.US Congressman Riley Moore said the proposed changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) amounted to "a clear attack against Christians" and urged India not to proceed with the legislation in its current form.In a post on X, the Republican Congressman from West Virginia said Christianity had a long history in India dating back to the arrival of St Thomas the Apostle on the Malabar Coast."But despite this long Christian history, India's Parliament is considering amending Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment (FCRA) rules to permit government takeovers of churches and religious charities," Moore wrote."This is a clear attack against Christians. If this bill proceeds in this way, it would be a point of major concern in our bilateral relationship with India," he added.The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 proposes the creation of a Designated Authority that would take over the management of foreign contributions and assets created using such funds if an organisation's FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or lapses after not being renewed.The Bill specifies that where such assets include a place of worship, the Designated Authority must ensure that its religious character is preserved.It also proposes reducing the maximum punishment for violations of the Act from five years' imprisonment to one year.The FCRA regulates the receipt and utilisation of foreign contributions by NGOs, charitable trusts, educational institutions, religious bodies and other associations. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, 13,520 organisations received foreign contributions worth Rs 55,741 crore between 2019 and 2022.Government data shows that as of July 15, 2026, there were 14,449 active FCRA registrations, while 22,498 had been cancelled and another 15,212 had expired.
Article Summary: US Congressman Riley Moore said the proposed changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) amounted to "a clear attack against Christians" Moore urged India not to proceed with the legislation in its current form. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, 13,520 organisations received foreign contributions worth Rs 55,741 crore between 2019 and 2022.

Article Title: Sudden drop in altitude: Flyers injured as Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight encounters turbulence
Article Text:
Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi experienced turbulence-related event during cruise. (Photo: TOI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Some passengers and crew members onboard Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight (AI 2379) suffered injuries when the aircraft encountered turbulence Tuesday morning, causing a sudden drop in altitude by 300 feet. An AI with medical support received the 134 passengers onboard the Airbus A320 on arrival just after 11 am. Over 10 passengers and two crew members are learnt to have been taken to the Medanta medical centre at the airport. Subsequently, 14 injured - 10 passengers and four crew members - were shifted to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram and India Spinal Injury Centre in Vasant Kunj.An AI spokesperson said the aircraft “experienced a brief in-flight turbulence-related event during cruise, resulting in a momentary change in altitude. The aircraft landed safely in Delhi and all passengers and crew have safely disembarked. There have been no serious injuries reported as of now. A small number of passengers and crew members with minor injuries requiring medical assessment have been taken to a medical facility at the airport for precautionary examination and care by Air India’s airport team and medical personnel.The A320 had taken off from Phuket at 8.27 am and landed in Delhi just after 11 am (all timings local).“The safety and well-being of our passengers and crew remain Air India’s highest priority. We are providing all necessary support to those affected and are cooperating fully with the relevant authorities as part of the investigation,” the spokesperson added.Aircraft frequently experience clear air turbulence (CAT), which International Civil Aviation Organisation defines as turbulence generated in clear air, in regions without clouds that is invisible to the pilot and by the US Federal Aviation Administration as sudden severe turbulence occurring in cloudless regions that causes violent buffeting of aircraft. Due to this possibility, it is advisable to have seatbelt loosely on during flight.
Article Summary: Some passengers and crew members onboard Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight suffered injuries. Aircraft encountered turbulence Tuesday morning, causing a sudden drop in altitude by 300 feet. Over 10 passengers and two crew members are learnt to have been taken to the Medanta medical centre at the airport. 14 injured were shifted to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram and India Spinal Injury Centre.

Article Title: '100% pure'? Stop misleading products' sale, FSSAI tells Dabur
Article Text:
FSSAI bars Dabur's 100 guarantee claims

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: If a food label says "100% pure", "100% natural" or "100% purity guaranteed", consumers may still need to read it with caution. In one of its strongest actions against misleading food labels, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has ordered Dabur India to stop selling a range of products carrying such claims, saying they violated food labelling regulations and could mislead buyers.The order covers products that include organic honey, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, cow ghee, coconut water and coconut milk, marketed with claims such as "100% juice", "100% purity" and "100% original".According to FSSAI, the company had made unauthorised organic claims, creating an impression of regulatory endorsement.The regulator also found that some claims on the labels were not permitted under Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.FSSAI has directed the company to immediately stop the sale of the identified products, recall products already in the market within 15 days and submit a compliance report.In a statement, Dabur said it believes the declarations on its product labels comply with the prevailing legal and regulatory framework and are consistent with long-standing industry practices. It said it stands by the purity and quality of its products and has never made misleading claims.Dabur said that it had begun removing the "100%" claims from product labels, advertisements and its website, in keeping with FSSAI's observations, adding that many products have already been updated while others are in the process of transition.It said that it is responding to the regulator, and will continue to engage constructively to resolve the matter.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India orders Dabur India to stop selling a range of products carrying such claims. The order covers products that include organic honey, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, cow ghee, coconut water and coconut milk. The company had made unauthorised organic claims, creating an impression of regulatory endorsement.

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha Tuesday passed Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill amid din, with MoS for home Nityanand Rai saying the legislation intends to ensure every child born is duly registered and also all deaths are registered "so that ghosts don't keep casting votes for parties that believe in appeasement".The bill was passed without any discussion and voice vote as an unrelenting opposition continued to disrupt proceedings over NEET-UG paper leak and Ram temple donation theft issues and demanding home minister Amit Shah's presence in the House.Responding to the discussion on the bill, Rai, in apparent reference to illegal immigrants, said, "The country now wants to get rid of ghosts. There are govts in some states that look for an opportunity and welcome those (who were not born in India) and register their births who are not eligible to be registered here. Now, we will not allow this to happen."The bill that was earlier passed by Lok Sabha seeks to tighten regulations for delayed registration of births and deaths and makes it mandatory to get approval from a judicial magistrate (first class) for cases reported more than two years after the event.Similar scenes also prevailed in LS, with it passing Appropriation Bill without discussion - the fifth legislation to be approved by voice vote in lower House in Parliament's monsoon session.Earlier, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman introduced Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill for passage, but it was left for another day as the House was adjourned for the day after passage of Appropriation Bill, which seeks to provide authorisation of appropriation of moneys out of Consolidated Fund of India to meet amounts spent on certain services during the financial year ended on March 31, 2023, in excess of the amounts granted.Monsoon session is heading for a virtual washout as both Houses have been repeatedly adjourned since the session began except for a discussion on the bill making punishment in paper leak cases more stringent. Article Title: Computer-based NEET? Govt tells SC decision after Nilekani report
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Centre Tuesday told Supreme Court that while the proposal to shift NEET from pen-and-paper mode to computer-based mode is under consideration, the final decision will be taken only after getting the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led high-powered task force set up to overhaul India's public examination systems.In an affidavit, govt briefed SC on measures taken to make the exam foolproof, including stringent penal provisions against use of unfair means and setting up of task force. It was responding to a plea by All India Medical Association seeking a more secure NEET following this year's paper leak.Govt said: "Migration from pen-and-paper mode to a computer-based mode, whether in single-stage or two-stage exam on the pattern of JEE, is presently under consideration by all stakeholders." The final approach, it added, would be adopted after considering the task force's recommendations.It said NTA has migrated seven of its eight major exams to computer-based testing. NEET (UG) remains its only major pen-and-paper exam.
Article Summary: Proposal to shift NEET from pen-and-paper mode to computer-based mode is under consideration. Final decision will be taken only after getting the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led high-powered task force set up to overhaul India's public examination systems.

Supreme Court urged prompt action against cyber fraudsters, while noting a reduction in incidents. Authorities were directed to expedite decisions on a 'kill switch' for phones. Monies transferred to mule accounts will be placed on hold by banks. Victims will receive recovered amounts expeditiously after investigations conclude. New directives aim to enhance cyber crime grievance redressal mechanisms.

NEW DELHI: Despite 75% reduction in cyber-crime and digital arrest incidents, Supreme Court continued to push authorities for prompt action against cyber fraudsters by issuing a slew of directives Tuesday, including an expeditious decision on a 'kill switch' in phones to prevent these crimes and placing on hold monies transferred to mule accounts.Attorney general R Venkataramani told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that number of complaints on national cyber crime portal had gone down from 1,23,672 in 2024 to 16,377 in 2026 (as of June 30). Besides, an Rs 18 crore has been restored to around 36,000 cyber fraud victims, he said in a status report.While appreciating the progress made in the matter, which the court is monitoring after taking suo motu cognisance on Oct 16 last year, bench directed Reserve Bank of India to formally "adopt and circulate formal standard operating procedure within four weeks detailing the action to be taken by banks for placing temporary hold on amounts and accounts in mule accounts linked to cyber fraud".Accepting a suggestion of amicus curiae N S Nappinai, SC also directed states, UTs and law enforcing agencies to take steps for expeditious adoption and operationalisation of grievance redressal and money restoration modules of home ministry, which should be given adequate publicity to enable victims to take required remedial measures.CJI-led bench directed "all adjudicatory authorities, including RBI ombudsman, consumer fora, courts and law enforcing authorities - to ensure that amounts recovered from fraudsters are disbursed to victims of digital arrest expeditiously".It asked RBI to file a status report on this aspect by Sept 16, the next date of hearing.Even as CBI continues investigations into digital scams, the court asked agency to examine AG's suggestion for lowering the present threshold of Rs 10 crore for taking up investigations into cases where the same gang of scamsters are involved."The proposal concerning a time-based 'Kill switch' for audio and video calls may be examined by ministry of information and technology, Department of Telecom and Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) in consultation with telecom intermediaries and a brief note on technical feasibility, efficacy, safeguards and alternatives be placed on record," the bench said.It asked Inter-Departmental Committee (IDC), which coordinates with various departments for steps to prevent digital arrest and cyber crime offences, to issue necessary directives on setting up of cyber crime grievance redressal mechanism and restoration of defrauded amounts to victims.
Article Summary: Supreme Court issues slew of directives against cyber fraudsters. Authorities directed to expedite decisions on a 'kill switch' for phones. Monies transferred to mule accounts will be placed on hold by banks. Victims will receive recovered amounts expeditiously after investigations conclude.

Article Title: Tie compensation to functional disability, says SC
Article Text:
The doctor certified her 90% disabled, but a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Holding that functional disability faced by a road accident victim should be the deciding factor for granting compensation and not doctor-certified medical disability, SC has granted compensation of Rs 83.3 lakh to a minor who met with an accident when she was just six months old and is now suffering from severe spinal cord and neurological injuries.Though the doctor certified her 90% disabled, a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability and quantified the compensation on that basis."...In the given facts of a case, a lesser physical disability may result in a much higher functional disability and in an appropriate case, even amount to complete loss of earning capacity," the bench said, adding it would be reasonable to assume that functional incapacity resulting out of a particular bodily injury may be higher and greater than what may be medically perceived."The present case concerns a child who has suffered permanent disability at a tender age and whose future stands altered on account of the injuries sustained in the accident. In such circumstances, the court is required to adopt an approach which is realistic, humane and consistent with the settled principles governing award of compensation under the MV Act," the bench said while increasing the amount of compensation to over Rs 83 lakh."Cases involving child victims suffering permanent or near total disability constitute a distinct and special category within the law relating to motor accident compensation. A child, by reason of age, vulnerability and complete dependence upon others, stands on an altogether different footing from an adult claimant. The consequences of a catastrophic injury suffered during childhood are not confined merely to the immediate physical impairment caused by the accident.Such injuries alter the entire course of the child's existence and affect every subsequent stage of her life. The law, therefore, cannot evaluate claims involving injured children through the same lens that may ordinarily be applied in cases involving adults," it said.
Article Summary: A minor who met with an accident when she was just six months old is now suffering from severe spinal cord and neurological injuries. Though the doctor certified her 90% disabled, a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability and quantified the compensation on that basis.

Article Title: From launch to data, tech to Isro facility, pvt firms to get 30-100% subsidy
Article Text:
New government schemes will offer significant financial support to Indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology transfer, and access to ISRO facilities. The programs are designed to lower entry barriers and accelerate private sector growth. This support will make satellite data and infrastructure more affordable for Indian entities.

BENGALURU: Indian private space companies and non-government entities will receive govt support ranging from 30% to 100% on everything from launch services and technology transfer to satellite data and access to Isro facilities under two new schemes of the Department of Space (DoS).The incentives — Launch Services Price-support Scheme (LSPS) and the Price Support Scheme — being implemented by Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) are aimed at lowering entry barriers, making Indian space businesses globally competitive and accelerating private participation across the sector.The larger of the two initiatives is the Launch Services Price-support Scheme, with a budget of Rs 800 crore over five years until June 2031. The scheme seeks to boost domestic commercial launch operations and strengthen India's position as a global launch hub.IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka told TOI: “The idea is to make the launches competitive. Therefore, we are trying to defray the cost of launch, thereby making the launch cost globally competitive. The ultimate beneficiary will be the satellite launch.”Under Category A, eligible entities can receive up to 50% support for using Isro and DoS launch facilities.The benefit extends to NGEs, government entities and launch vehicle providers.Category B offers a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower, for Indian small launch vehicles carrying satellites, experiments or payloads weighing up to 500 kg. The support is available to satellite owners and operators.The subsidy would apply to launches by Indian private entities from Indian soil too. “It will be applicable to [Skyroot’s] Vikram also. Any satellite launch by an Indian company... from Indian soil... we will directly pay the satellite guys $3,000 per kg,” Goenka said. He added that the policy is focused on promoting small launch vehicles where private sector participation is growing.Category C provides the highest level of support, offering 100% funding for repurposed upper-stage platforms carrying payloads of up to 120 kg. The funding is capped at $13,000 per kg and limited to four missions. The category is aimed at NGEs, govt entities and launch vehicle providers.Category D extends launch incentives to satellites weighing up to 100 kg launched aboard PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 missions. Beneficiaries will receive a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower.Complementing the launch incentives is a separate Price Support Scheme for Indian entities, which will run for three years until Feb 2029. The programme is intended to reduce the cost of accessing India’s space infrastructure, technologies and data.The scheme has three components. The first provides up to 50% support for the utilisation of DoS and In-SPACe facilities, along with technical expertise.The second offers a 30% subsidy on Technology Transfer Fees (TTF) for technologies licensed from Isro, lowering the cost for companies seeking to commercialise govt-developed technologies.The third provides a 50% subsidy on standard Earth Observation data and data products, making satellite imagery and geospatial datasets more affordable for Indian companies developing applications in agriculture, urban planning, disaster management, climate services and other downstream sectors.
Article Summary: New government schemes will offer significant financial support to Indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology transfer, and access to ISRO facilities. The programs are designed to lower entry barriers and accelerate private sector growth.

Article Title: For every Rs 100 India spends on R&D, govt gives Rs 48, pvt Rs 45
Article Text:
The balance of research and development funding has shifted, with government and private industry now investing nearly the same amount. In recent years, private sector contributions to research have seen a notable rise. Government spending is concentrated on sectors deemed strategic and beneficial to the public. Additionally, multinational corporations are increasingly influential in shaping India's research environment, although the overall research intensity still lags behind other major economies.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: For every Rs 100 spent on R&D, the govt contributes about Rs 48 while private industry accounts for Rs 45, latest data from R&D Statistics At a Glance 2025-26 by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), shows.The remaining Rs 7 comes from scientific and industrial research organisations (SIROs) and private higher education institutions.India’s Gross Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD) breached Rs 2.4-lakh crore in 2023-24, more than three times the Rs 79,356 crore recorded a decade ago. However, overall R&D spend is still under 1% of the GDP, touching 0.8%, as per the latest figures.Private industry’s share in GERD increased from 39.7% in 2020-21 to 45.2% in 2023-24 in just three years. During the same period, govt share declined from 54.5% to 48.2%, although it continues to remain the country’s single largest contributor to research spending.The report notes that private R&D expenditure has been growing at an average annual rate of around 20% over the last three years.While the DST report’s detailed analysis is up to 2023-24, it has projected overall trends for two more years: “The upward [spending] trend is expected to continue, with GERD projected to reach nearly Rs 2.8-lakh-crore by 2024-25 and more than Rs 3.1-lakh-crore crore by 2025–26,” it reads.Govt spending continues to be concentrated in strategic and public-interest sectors. Among the Centre’s scientific agencies, DRDO accounted for 32.7%, followed by the Department of Space (15%), Department of Atomic Energy (14.4%), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (13.1%) and Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (8.7%). Together, 12 major scientific agencies accounted for 76% of govt R&D spend.Transportation emerged as the biggest destination for industrial R&D, accounting for 32.6% of private sector expenditure, followed by pharmaceuticals (21.4%), biotechnology (8.6%), IT (7.9%) and electrical and electronics (5.9%).The report also highlights the growing role of MNCs in India’s research landscape. Their share in business R&D expenditure has increased from 49.9% in 2020-21 to 71.3% in 2023-24. According to the report, the growth rate of R&D expenditure has outpaced GDP growth after 2021-22, except in 2022-23, reflecting the increasing priority accorded to research and innovation.Despite the encouraging trends, India continues to trail many major economies in research intensity. At 0.8% of GDP, the country's R&D expenditure remains below that of China (2.6%), Brazil (1.2%) and several advanced economies that invest more than 2% of their GDP in research.Nevertheless, the latest figures point to a maturing innovation ecosystem where the burden of financing research is gradually shifting from being overwhelmingly government-led to one in which private enterprise is emerging as an almost equal partner.
Article Summary: India’s Gross Expenditure on Research and Development breached Rs 2.4-lakh crore in 2023-24. For every Rs 100 spent on R&D, the govt contributes about Rs 48 while private industry accounts for Rs 45. Government spending is concentrated on sectors deemed strategic and beneficial to the public.

Article Title: Big clean energy milestone: NPCIL cumulatively generates over 1,000 bn units of N-power, avoids 860 million tons of CO2 emissions
Article Text:
India has achieved a remarkable milestone in clean energy, generating over one thousand billion units from nuclear power. This achievement helps avoid more than 860 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions. The government aims to increase nuclear power capacity to 100 GW by 2047, with an intermediate target of 22 GW by 2031-32. This expansion will involve multiple stakeholders and the introduction of new legislation.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a milestone for India’s clean energy production, Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) has cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of nuclear electricity.NPCIL said Tuesday, “Since commencement of commercial operation, NPCIL’s nuclear power plants have cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of clean electricity, thereby avoiding over 860 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions into the environment.”“This milestone reflects NPCIL’s steadfast commitment to deliver safe, reliable and sustainable nuclear power, strengthening India’s energy security while supporting the nation’s clean energy transition and climate goals,” it said on XTo give the scale of how much carbon emission is avoided, a typical passenger vehicle emits about 4.6 metric tonnes of CO2 per year. Avoiding 860 million tonnes is equal to taking roughly 187 million gasoline-powered cars going off the road for an entire year. At least 860 million tonnes is roughly equivalent to the total annual greenhouse gas emissions of a major industrial country like Germany or Japan for a full year.Govt has drawn up a roadmap for reaching the 100 GW nuclear power capacity in the next two decades by 2047, as announced in the Nuclear Energy Mission in the Budget 2025-26, thereby increasing the share of reliable, low-carbon base-load nuclear energy in the country’s energy mix and reaching the goal of net zero carbon emissions by 2070.The present nuclear power capacity of 8.78 GW is expected to reach about 22 GW by 2031-32 on progressive completion of projects presently at various stages of implementation. Another 32 GW of nuclear power capacity is envisaged to be set up beyond 2032 by NPCIL under the administrative control of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE).This will comprise indigenous pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and light water reactors (LWRs) planned to be set up by 2047, taking NPCIL’s nuclear power capacity to 54 GW.The balance of 46 GW comprising reactors of different technologies, is expected to be set up by other public sector enterprises, private sector and joint ventures in different business models. With the govt enacting the SHANTI Act (Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India Act, 2025) last year, the new law provides the legal framework that makes this 46 GW expansion possible.
Article Summary: Government aims to increase nuclear power capacity to 100 GW by 2047. NPCIL’s nuclear power plants have cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of clean electricity, thereby avoiding over 860 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions into the environment.

Article Title: MPs feel left out of foundation stone laying, parliamentary panel steps in

NEW DELHI: A parliamentary panel in its report among various concerns pertaining to the centrally-sponsored rural road scheme PMGSY has brought into focus that despite advisories from the rural development ministry, MPs are often not invited for foundation laying and inauguration ceremonies.This, the committee observed, “undermines established parliamentary protocol”.To deal with the situation, Standing Committee on Rural Development and Panchayati Raj chaired by Congress MP Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka in its report tabled in Parliament Friday recommended that department of rural development (DoRD) “issue strict mandatory instructions” to state govts and authorities to invite the MP concerned or their representative at least 15 days in advance through multiple modes of communication like email, letter, and SMS.“High-quality photographs of the events, clearly depicting the MP’s participation along with the plaque, must be mandatorily uploaded on the Online Monitoring, Management and Accounting System (OMMAS) within seven days of the ceremony,” the panel has recommended.It suggested instituting a quarterly monitoring mechanism to track compliance, linking persistent violations to administrative accountability, and conducting regular sensitisation programmes for officials for effective implementation of the 2022 advisory and enforcement of these protocols.These findings are part of the action taken on the recommendations made the panel in its 17th report on “Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)” (2024-25), in which it was highlighted that the committee has been frequently informed about the violation of norms/provisions of PMGSY pertaining to the protocol with regards to MPs.In the action taken reply, the ministry shared its advisory, dated Feb 2, 2022, with regard to invitation to the public representatives for foundation laying and inauguration ceremonies of PMGSY works. The committee has acknowledged the reply but called for measures to ensure compliance.
Article Summary: A parliamentary panel has called attention to the frequent exclusion of MPs from events related to rural road schemes. MPs are often not invited for foundation laying and inauguration ceremonies. This, the committee observed, “undermines established parliamentary protocol’

NEW DELHI: The Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation, whose student wing All India Students Association (AISA) was at the forefront in the Cockroach Janta Party led protests at Jantar Mantar, has demanded that the voting age should be lowered to 16 from 18 years to empower the younger lot among Gen Z.This comes in the backdrop of the students protests that succeeded in getting Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign. For the Left parties like CPI(ML)L, the victory of their student outfits in raising the issues affecting Gen Z, has emboldened them and provided an opportunity to connect with the students to take up their concerns related to education, employment and accountability.Attacking the govt over its use of force against protesters, CPI(ML) L general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya said, “In the protests at Jantar Mantar the world saw an awakening where Gen Z came out to talk about the things that affect them and sought accountability. I feel they are ready and therefore I feel voting age must be lowered,” Bhattacharya said.The voting age in India was brought down from 21 to 18 years through ‘The Constitution (Sixty-first Amendment) Act, 1988. While in most countries the age of voting is 18, in some countries like Argentina, Austria, Brazil, Cuba, Ecuador, Nicaragua, East Timor, Greece, and Indonesia 16 or 17 year olds can vote.Bhattacharya in a statement released by the party on Tuesday said that if the RSS really wants to listen to India’s Gen Z, they should lower the voting age to 16.In today's digital era of information revolution, 16-year-olds are informed enough to make their political choices,” he said.“RSS is reportedly quite desperate to reach out to Gen Z. Mohan Bhagwat is all set to address 2,000 students aged 15 to 19 brought from 100 cities on August 6 at Mumbai’s Nita Mukesh Ambani Centre! The numbers are impressive, but what will be the outreach about?,” Bhattacharya asked.“Modi (PM Narendra Modi) has already talked about ‘culture shock’, invoking patriarchal prejudices against India’s ‘misled daughters’. The orchestrated backlash, both online and offline, is forcing 15-year-olds to offer apology videos,” he alleged.With this attack on the ruling dispensation, CPI(ML)L has set the pitch for its outreach to Gen Z. “In the protests at Jantar Mantar the world saw an awakening where Gen Z came out to talk about the things that affect them and sought accountability. I feel they are ready and therefore I feel voting age must be lowered,” Bhattacharya said.He said that since he raised the demand on Tuesday, he has received positive responses from the youth. Bhattacharya plans to not only discuss this with AISA members but also take it up with Left parties - CPI(M) and CPI(ML) and also INDIA bloc members.Meanwhile, all set to keep up the momentum generated by the protests, the Left parties CPM, CPI(ML)L and CPI are working on stepping up coordination for the outreach among various sections at the grassroots including students. "The Left needs to coordinate with more focus as a group on issues and align with movements led by students, workers, women and farmers across states. To enable this we are working on a plan and a series of meetings have been held to discuss how we can improve coordination," Bhattacharya said.
Article Summary: The Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation has demanded that the voting age should be lowered to 16 from 18 years. NEW DELHI: Govt’s rooftop solar initiative, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, has crossed the 50-lakh household milestone within 29 months of its launch in Feb 2024, achieving half of its target of one crore households by March 2027.According to new and renewable energy ministry, more than five lakh households installed rooftop solar plants in July, the highest monthly addition since the scheme began. So far, nearly 19 lakh households have recorded zero electricity bills in at least one billing cycle, significantly reducing their power expenses.The ministry said more than 12 lakh households earned a combined Rs 421 crore by selling surplus electricity to the grid in FY 2024-25, translating into an additional income of around Rs 3,500 a year per household.Cumulatively, 14.8 GW of rooftop solar capacity has been commissioned under the scheme so far.The ministry said 1.6 lakh installations have been completed for Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana beneficiaries, Below Poverty Line families, and SC/ST households across four states under the utility-led aggregation model. The model enables low-income households to install rooftop solar systems while helping states reduce their power subsidy burden.Govt has also solarised 25,255 govt buildings with a combined rooftop solar capacity of 872 MW, against 41,542 buildings where installations totalling 1,418 MW are considered feasible. Overall, states have identified around 3.2 lakh govt buildings with an estimated rooftop solar potential of 4,400 MW. Of these, 81,329 buildings with a combined capacity of 1,450 MW have already been solarised, the ministry said.

Article Title: Child protection panel launches inquiry into Meta over alleged child sexual abuse material ads

In response, the child rights organization has demanded clarity from Meta Platforms Inc. Furthermore, the NHRC has instructed the Delhi Police to look into these troubling assertions, as both entities scrutinize Meta's adherence to child protection regulations.

Initiates formal inquiry

NEW DELHI: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has decided to institute an inquiry into allegations that advertisements related to Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) appeared on Meta-owned platforms, government sources said on Tuesday.The move comes after the child rights body took suo motu cognisance of a BBC Eye report last month alleging that advertisements on Instagram promoted child sexual abuse material.NCPCR had issued a notice to Meta Platforms Inc. on July 3 seeking an explanation, to which the company responded a week later.Following an examination of Meta's reply, the Commission has now decided to initiate a formal inquiry "to determine the facts of the matter", sources said.Separately, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) had directed the Delhi Police to conduct a comprehensive probe into the allegations and examine whether Meta and other entities complied with mandatory reporting obligations under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.The NHRC took cognisance of the BBC World Service report, which alleged that paid advertisements on Instagram used specific keywords and redirected users to channels where child sexual abuse material was allegedly being offered for sale.In a letter dated July 8, the Commission asked the Delhi Police Commissioner to submit a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR). It later sent a reminder on July 29, seeking submission of the pending report.Earlier today, IT Secretary S Krishnan said that the Centre will raise a range of concerns with Meta's global team during its meeting in India on August 5 and 6, including the platform's handling of Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM), the temporary restriction of prominent verified accounts, and the spread of AI-generated content.
Article Summary: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has decided to institute an inquiry into allegations that advertisements related to Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) appeared on Meta-owned platforms. The move comes after the child rights body took suo motu cognisance of a BBC report last month alleging that advertisements on Instagram promoted child sexual abuse material.

Article Title: ‘No insurance, no fuel’: SC directs govt to prepare pilot project, flags 16.54 crore uninsured vehicles
Article Text:
SC has raised alarm on the uninsured vehicles operating on road

16.54 crore vehicles uninsured

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Centre to evolve a pilot project under which vehicles without valid third-party insurance could be denied fuel at petrol pumps until they obtain the mandatory insurance cover.A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Prashant Kumar Mishra took note of the large number of uninsured vehicles on Indian roads and said nearly 56% of vehicles remain uninsured, citing the Report of the Standing Committee on Finance 2024-25.The court directed the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), in consultation with the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), to deliberate and evolve a pilot project linking fuel supply to a vehicle's valid insurance status.“As deliberated upon in court, the IRDA (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority) in consultation with the MoRTH (Ministry of Road Transport and Highways) to deliberate and evolve a pilot project whereby fuel for vehicles to be linked with valid insurance status. In the absence thereof, the vehicle concerned would be refused fuel at petrol pumps, until such time that valid insurance is obtained,” the bench said.The court said denying fuel to uninsured vehicles could help identify uninsured or unregistered vehicles and encourage owners to obtain valid insurance.“Such projects would ensure ground-level compliance with the statutory mandate of Section 146 of the MVA. This may be done through the use of ANPR (Automatic Number Plate Recognition) cameras,” it said. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the court noted, has “in principle, no objection” to the proposal.The Supreme Court also directed that the mandatory third-party insurance period for newly purchased vehicles be extended.In 2018, the court had mandated third-party insurance for three years for new cars and five years for new two-wheelers at the time of purchase or registration.“We notice that despite eight years having passed from the said direction, a large number of vehicles remain uninsured,” the bench observed.It directed that third-party insurance henceforth be purchased for four years for new cars and six years for new two-wheelers, and directed IRDAI to issue the necessary directions immediately.The court said 16.54 crore out of 30.48 crore vehicles were uninsured, describing the figure as “stark”.It said the lack of insurance can delay or defeat the statutory safeguard of compensation for road accident victims.“The object behind mandatory insurance under Section 146 of the MVA is not just that victims of road accidents are compensated, it is also that they are not drawn into prolonged litigation,” the bench said.It noted that uninsured vehicles often leave accident victims and their families facing prolonged litigation over the quantum and liability for compensation. The impact, it said, is particularly severe when a victim dies or suffers permanent disability.The court also directed IRDAI and MoRTH to deploy ANPR cameras in certain states, integrating them with data from the Insurance Information Bureau and the VAHAN portal.The system is intended to enable automatic issuance of e-challans to uninsured vehicles.The court also directed that state police be provided with handheld devices or downloadable applications linked to the Insurance Information Bureau and VAHAN data to verify the insurance status of vehicles in real time.“This is to monitor real-time insurance status of vehicles and impose challans for violations, ensuring compliance with mandatory insurance on the ground,” the court said.The court further directed IRDAI to provide private vehicle owners with various policy options, including add-on covers, personal accident cover and own-damage cover, alongside a base policy offering the minimum coverage required under the Motor Vehicles Act.The court also took note of road accidents on national highways and the problem of long queues at toll plazas. It directed the Centre to implement pilot projects on selected corridors to replace stopping at toll plazas with automatic detection of vehicles passing through toll points.The directions were issued in a motor accident claim case, with the court observing that compliance with the statutory requirement for third-party motor vehicle insurance remains inadequate despite the existing legal framework.It said accident victims and their families often have to “run from pillar to post” to receive compensation.
Article Summary: Supreme Court has raised alarm on the uninsured vehicles operating on Indian roads. 16.54 crore out of 30.48 crore vehicles were uninsured, describing the figure as ‘stark’ The court also directed that the mandatory third-party insurance period for newly purchased vehicles be extended.

Article Title: Farmers back ethanol in meeting with agriculture minister, say it will boost income, secure energy

NEW DELHI: A group of farmers on Tuesday voiced support for ethanol during a meeting with Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan at Krishi Bhawan, amid general protests against the use of the E20 bio-fuel mix in vehicles, saying ethanol would increase farmers’ income and secure the country’s energy.Chouhan told them that the central govt’s thinking was clear that the benefit of the ethanol programme should reach the entire chain from the field to the fuel tank, but the biggest share should go in the interest of the farmer.The farmers, under the banner of the Akhil Bharatiya Kisan Samanvay Samiti, told the minister that ethanol was a big opportunity for farming, provided its policy was farmer-centric and the right price of the crop reached the farmer directly.In India, sugarcane contributes to 30-35% of total ethanol production while the remaining 65-70% is derived from grains such as maize and rice.Farmers from Punjab, Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu were present at the meeting. They insisted that the real benefit of the ethanol programme should go to the farmer, not only to companies or middlemen.They said that with ethanol, farm produce would not remain limited to the mandis, but would reach petrol pumps and the energy market, creating a new and stronger market for farmers.They told the minister that if ethanol was made from sugarcane, maize, rice and other feedstock, farmers would get more buyers, and crop spoilage or storage problems would be reduced.Extending their full support for ethanol, they said it was necessary that whether it was maize or sugarcane, farmers should get proper prices for any crop. Farmer representatives said, “We want the ethanol policy to create a new path for farming, not a new worry for us.We are with ethanol, if ethanol also stays with us.”The farmers demanded that the agriculture ministry and farmer organisations should jointly explain clearly which crops would benefit from ethanol and how, and how a shift could be made from water-intensive crops to drought-tolerant crops.Chouhan assured that the policy would be reviewed to maintain a balance in the prices and demand of maize, rice, sugarcane and other feedstock. He said decisions would be taken only from the perspective of farmer interest, especially the benefit of maize farmers. He added that the negative narrative on ethanol would be countered through scientific studies and technical reports, and a fact-based dialogue would be carried out in partnership with farmers.
Article Summary: Farmers from Punjab, Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu were present at the meeting. They insisted that the real benefit of the ethanol programme should go to the farmer, not only to companies or middlemen.

During this auspicious time, devotees arrive in large numbers at the Binsar Mahadev Temple, nestled in the lap of the dense cedar forests of Ranikhet (Almora), seeking faith, devotion, and spiritual peace.This region not only offers the pilgrims a divine experience but also a unique communion with nature. NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday observed that State Bar Councils have increasingly become “men’s clubs” and said the monopoly over their representation and functioning must be dismantled.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the remarks while hearing petitions related to elections to the Bar Council of India and State Bar Councils.“Bar Councils have become men’s clubs. We may observe that people take it like a monopoly. This has to be completely dismantled,” CJI Surya Kant remarked during the hearing.The court directed the Chief Justices of the jurisdictional High Courts to nominate two women members to every State Bar Council through co-option. One must be a former woman High Court judge and the other a senior woman advocate with a fair standing at the Bar.The court said the nominated members should have no connection with the election process so that they can function independently and impartially.“As far as co-option is concerned...10% we always had in mind. There should be co-option of those who don't have anything to do with elections,” the court observed.The Supreme Court also clarified that a woman who unsuccessfully contested a State Bar Council election would not be barred from being considered for co-option.The court referred the issue of the methodology for calculating transferable votes, particularly for women candidates, to the High-Powered Supervisory Committee headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia. The committee will reconsider the methodology after inviting suggestions from members of the Bar and giving them an opportunity for an oral hearing.The Supreme Court had earlier directed that women should have 30 per cent% representation in State Bar Councils, with 20 per cent of the seats filled through direct elections and the remaining 10 per cent through co-option where required.The High-Powered Supervisory Committee was constituted by the court to oversee elections to the Bar Council of India and State Bar Councils and deal with election-related disputes.

Article Title: From Hype To Help: How AI Is Solving India's Real Problems
Article Text:
AI is increasingly being used to tackle some of the country's most persistent development challenges.

Govts, tech companies, startups, nonprofits and research organisations are working together to deploy AI where it can reach millions of people rather than a handful of users.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

AI is often discussed in terms of chatbots, coding assistants, and workplace productivity. But a quieter transformation is taking shape across India, where AI is increasingly being used to tackle some of the country's most persistent development challenges, from helping farmers cope with climate change to assisting teachers in rural classrooms, improving TB screening and making govt services available in multiple languages.According to MeitY, India’s digital economy contributed Rs 31.6 lakh crore, or 11.7% of the GDP, in 2022-23. By 2030, that share is expected to approach one-fifth of the economy. Increasingly, govts, tech companies, startups, nonprofits and research organisations are working together to deploy AI where it can reach millions of people rather than a handful of users.Education offers one of the clearest examples. Microsoft’s Shiksha Copilot, developed with the Shikshana Foundation using Azure OpenAI Service, is helping around 1,000 teachers prepare localised lesson plans for nearly 30,000 children across 750 govt schools in Karnataka.What once took teachers hours can now be done in about 10 minutes. The programme is expected to expand to another 8,000 teachers across Karnataka and Telangana. The company has also announced a larger commitment to train 10 million Indians in AI by 2030 after achieving its earlier target of skilling 2 million people ahead of schedule.Agriculture has emerged as another major beneficiary. Farmers increasingly face unpredictable rainfall, pest outbreaks, and rising temperatures, while agricultural extension services remain stretched.AI-powered advisory platforms help bridge that gap.Farmer.Chat, developed by Digital Green, provides advice through voice, text, images and videos in local languages. It offers recommendations tailored to crops, soils, weather, and local conditions. The platform reportedly expanded from 15,000 to 250,000 Indian users within a year while costing less than$1 per farmer annually. Digital Green also says it has reduced the cost of introducing a new farming practice from $35 to under $1 by using AI-driven advisory systems.Non-profit institute Wadhwani AI uses similar technologies at a larger systems level. Its AI tools are now reported to have reached more than 190 million people. The organisation says its solutions have helped prioritise over 35,000 villages for tuberculosis screening, supported nearly 2.7 lakh teachers, delivered personalised learning support to 7.9 million students and resolved more than 5 million agricultural grievances.Healthcare is seeing practical applications. Startup Qure.ai has developed an AI system that analyses chest X-rays for tuberculosis. A Health Technology Assessment by the Indian Institute of Public Health Gandhinagar reportedly found the technology to be more cost-effective than conventional screening pathways. That could be significant in a country that accounts for nearly 28% of the world's new tuberculosis cases.And, language is a barrier AI is beginning to address. Platforms such as Bhashini aim to make govt services accessible in more than 22 Indian languages. AI-powered translation is already being used for grievance redressal, Aadhaar transliteration, railway enquiries and several citizen services, reducing dependence on English or Hindi and making digital governance more inclusive.Climate resilience is becoming another area of rapid innovation. SatSure combines AI with satellite imagery to help banks assess agricultural loans, monitor climate risks, and evaluate farms. The company says its systems operate across more than 70,000 villages, reducing loan underwriting time while improving assessments for farmers who often lack formal credit histories.India is also investing heavily in the infrastructure needed to support this ecosystem. Enterprise AI adoption is estimated at 87%, while the IndiaAI Mission has expanded national computing capacity to 38,000 GPUs under an outlay exceeding Rs 10,300 crore. Nearly universal 5G coverage, digital public infrastructure such as AgriStack and a growing climate-tech startup ecosystem are providing the foundations for wider AI deployment.The common thread across these initiatives is not the sophistication of the algorithms but their ability to solve everyday problems at scale.
Article Summary: AI is increasingly being used to tackle some of the country's most persistent development challenges. It is helping farmers cope with climate change, assisting teachers in rural classrooms, improving TB screening and making govt services available in multiple languages. India is also investing heavily in the infrastructure needed to support this ecosystem.

NEW DELHI: The Punjab Assembly on Tuesday passed a resolution opposing the Centre's E20 ethanol-blended fuel policy, expressing concern that the use of E20 fuel could damage vehicles that are not compatible with the higher ethanol blend.Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema moved the resolution on the second day of the monsoon session of the Assembly, questioning why the Centre advanced the rollout of the E20 fuel policy to 2026 instead of its earlier target of 2030.He also alleged that the BJP-led Union government had implemented the policy under pressure from the United States, the the Assemblies of Gujarat, Goa and Jammu and Kashmir.The party has also held an "Ethanol Town Hall" and launched a nationwide signature campaign against the policy, arguing that vehicle owners should Article Title: SC orders nationwide action against 'digital arrest' scams; tells RBI to share SOP on 'mule accounts'

The Supreme Court, on Tuesday, directed banks, financial intermediaries, regulators and law enforcement agencies to work together to curb the rising menace of "digital arrest" scams and improve the recovery of money lost to cyber fraud.Hearing a suo motu matter ‘In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents', the court called for a coordinated institutional response, including faster grievance redressal, stronger mechanisms to restore victims' money and wider public awareness campaigns.The apex court directed the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to formulate a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on mule accounts within four weeks, PTI cites.Mule accounts are bank accounts used by cybercriminals to receive, transfer or route money obtained through fraud. The court said stronger systems are needed to identify, freeze and prevent the misuse of such accounts.The Supreme Court has also directed all states to operationalise cyber fraud grievance redressal and money restoration mechanisms so that complaints can be acted upon promptly and recovery efforts can begin without delay.The apex court directed the Centre to examine the feasibility of creating a shared liability and victim compensation framework for cyber fraud cases.The court also asked an Inter-Departmental Committee to consult banks and financial intermediaries on measures to tackle digital arrest scams. It said institutions must work together to detect fraudulent transactions early and improve the chances of recovering money for victims.The step comes a week after the Supreme Court suggested that the Centre consider formally defining 'digital arrest' as a separate offence under criminal law, with stringent penalties for those found guilty.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has directed banks, financial intermediaries, regulators and law enforcement agencies to work together to curb the rising menace of 'digital arrest' scams.
