Article Title: 'Likely to mislead': FSSAI bars Dabur from selling products with '100%' guarantee claims
Article Text:
Food regulator FSSAI prohibited Dabur from selling many products.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has prohibited Dabur India from selling several food products carrying "100 per cent" claims, saying such labelling are "ambiguous, unverifiable" and "likely to mislead consumers".In a post on social media on Monday, the food regulator said it had issued a prohibition order to Dabur India Ltd over the sale of products carrying claims such as "100 per cent Natural", "100 per cent Pure", "100 per cent Purity Guaranteed", "100 per cent Organic" and "100 per cent Tender Coconut Water".The products covered under the order include honey, cow ghee, edible oils, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, coconut water, coconut milk and other food items.According to the FSSAI, the use of such claims violates the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising & Claims) Regulations, 2018, as they are "ambiguous, unverifiable and likely to mislead consumers.""Food products being sold on the company's website were found carrying misleading '100 per cent' claims such as '100 per cent Natural', '100 per cent Pure', '100 per cent Purity Guaranteed', '100 per cent Organic' and '100 per cent Tender Coconut Water'," the regulator said.The FSSAI also found that Dabur Himalayan Organic Apple Cider Vinegar and Dabur Organic Honey displayed the Jaivik Bharat logo without a valid FSSAI organic endorsement.In addition, Dabur Hommade Coconut Milk was marketed with the claim "100 per cent Purity", which the regulator said is not permitted for compound food products under the advertising and claims regulations.The regulator said it had earlier issued a notice directing Dabur to discontinue the misleading claims, but "no satisfactory corrective action was taken by Dabur.""FSSAI directed Dabur India Limited to immediately prohibit the sale of the food products identified in the notice and all other food products carrying misleading '100%' claims, and to submit an Action Taken Report (ATR) within 15 days," the regulator said.Responding to the development, Dabur India said it is reviewing the notice. "We have received the FSSAI notice and are in the process of checking the content mentioned in the notice on our website," the company said in a statement.The action is part of the regulator's broader crackdown on misleading food labelling and advertising. Over the past few months, the FSSAI has increasingly used social media to publicise enforcement action against food business operators and e-commerce platforms selling such products.
Article Summary: Food regulator FSSAI prohibits Dabur India from selling many products. Products covered include honey, cow ghee, edible oils, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, coconut water, coconut milk and other food items. The action is part of a broader crackdown on misleading food labelling and advertising.

Article Title: Centre summons Meta's global team on August 5-6 to raise CSAM, AI concerns
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Centre will raise a range of concerns with Meta's global team during its meeting in India on August 5 and 6, including the platform's handling of Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM), the temporary restriction of prominent verified accounts, and the spread of AI-generated content, IT Secretary S Krishnan said on Tuesday.Meta has been under regulatory scrutiny over Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) in paid advertisements on Instagram, and the government had earlier issued a notice to the company over the issue.The move comes days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook post addressing students' concerns over paper leaks was removed briefly."There are a range of issues... the CSAM issue was raised, so what measures have been taken regarding that, and synthetically generated information ... to what extent that is being looked at. Then, of course, for prominent personalities, when they have verified accounts, if content has to be taken down, there have to be safeguards... all of these will be the issues," Krishnan told reporters on the sidelines of the launch of an independent multimodal AI evaluation platform by AI4Bharat at IIT Madras and Josh Talks AI.He said the government wants to understand why Meta's systems have failed in these instances and what challenges the company is facing."We would like to understand from them (Meta) as to why some of these things have not been working the way they are supposed to work, and what are the challenges," Krishnan said.The IT secretary added that as one of the world's leading technology companies, Meta should have the technological capability to address such issues effectively.The government had earlier summoned Meta India officials and later sought an explanation from the company's global team over the temporary restriction on the Prime Minister's post.The Centre has also accused the social media giant of displaying algorithmic bias.
Article Summary: The Centre will raise a range of concerns with Meta's global team during its meeting in India on August 5 and 6. Meta has been under regulatory scrutiny over Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) The government had earlier issued a notice to the company over the issue.

Article Title: Weather tomorrow: IMD forecasts of heavy rain across several states; thunderstorms, lightning likely
Article Text:

Uttar Pradesh weather tomorrow

Himachal Pradesh weather tomorrow

Kerala weather tomorrow

Delhi-NCR weather tomorrow

IMD's latest forecast for the next few days





NEW DELHI: Heavy rainfall is expected to continue across several states over the next few days, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting intense showers, thunderstorms and lightning in parts of Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh and the Northeast, also predicted extremely heavy rain over parts of Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya, which could affect neighbouring districts of Assam.The IMD has forecast extremely heavy rainfall, accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning, over parts of Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya over the next few days. The weather system could impact Assam districts bordering the two states, including Charaideo, Sivasagar, Jorhat and Golaghat. A yellow alert has also been issued for parts of Nagaland.Heavy rain is likely at isolated places across eastern and western Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday. Widespread rain and thundershowers are expected to continue, with heavy showers likely in parts of the state through August 6. While eastern Uttar Pradesh may continue to receive isolated heavy rain on August 7, no heavy rain warning has been issued for western Uttar Pradesh on that day.The weather office has forecast widespread rainfall across Himachal Pradesh until August 7. On Wednesday, heavy rain is likely at isolated places in Bilaspur, Hamirpur, Kangra and Shimla.The IMD has advised travellers, especially those visiting hilly areas, to remain cautious as heavy rain, low clouds and mist could reduce visibility.Kerala is expected to continue receiving heavy rainfall on Wednesday. The IMD has also warned of thunderstorms, lightning, squally weather and strong surface winds across parts of the state. Similar weather conditions are likely to persist until August 8.No major weather warning has been issued for Delhi-NCR in the latest forecast. However, residents can expect generally cloudy skies with the possibility of light rain or thunderstorms in some areas.The southwest monsoon remains active over large parts of the country, bringing widespread rainfall to central, northern and northeastern India. According to the IMD, wet weather is likely to continue across several states over the next few days.
Article Summary: Heavy rainfall is expected to continue across several states over the next few days. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast intense showers, thunderstorms and lightning in parts of Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh and the Northeast. The weather system could impact Assam districts bordering the two states.

Article Title: 'In every national security decision, Doval had a role': Amit Shah praises NSA at award ceremony
Article Text:
Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security

'First selection' after Modi became PM

Shah invokes Lokmanya Tilak's legacy

'Award will inspire those who serve the nation'

Doval accepts award with humility

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval for his contribution to India's national security and foreign policy, saying the veteran intelligence officer has played a crucial role behind every major national security decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.Speaking at a function in Pune after presenting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to Doval, Shah said the NSA's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening India's security architecture and defence preparedness.He also said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him."NSA Ajit Doval has played a great role in strengthening India's foreign policy. In every decision of PM Modi for national security, Doval has had a 'role and advice' in the background," Shah said."Whenever history is written, if anyone analyses internal security and external security, then clearly, for Ajit Doval ji, a golden page will have to be kept reserved; there is no doubt about this," he added.Shah said one of the first decisions taken by PM Modi after assuming office in 2014 was appointing Doval as the National Security Advisor, a move he said transformed India's strategic posture."Today, India's foreign policy has become a foreign policy with a backbone of steel; no one can deny this. We have, along with self-respect, strengthened our position in the world," Shah said.Praising Doval's decades-long career in the Intelligence Bureau, Shah said India has emerged as a stronger and more confident nation under Modi's leadership, with Doval making a significant contribution to that transformation."After becoming NSA in 2014, Doval helped implement many strategic ideas on the ground and played a major role in modernising India's armed forces, strengthening technology, enhancing operational capability and improving the country's defence preparedness," Shah said.He added that the Modi government has fundamentally transformed both the defensive and offensive capabilities of the armed forces over the past 12 years, with Doval playing a key role in the process.Shah also noted that much of Doval's contribution can never be made public because of the confidential nature of intelligence operations.Recalling his tenure as Gujarat's home minister, Shah narrated how he first interacted with Doval following the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts. He said then chief minister Narendra Modi had advised Gujarat Police to consult Doval while investigating the attacks."I remember Ajit ji had come to my house. The tips he gave resulted in Gujarat Police resolving not just the Ahmedabad bomb blast, but 13 bomb blasts across the country all at once. This was a very great achievement," Shah said.The Union home minister also paid tribute to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, calling him one of the foremost architects of India's freedom movement.He said Tilak's iconic slogan, "Swarajya is my birthright, and I shall have it," gave a new direction to India's freedom struggle and inspired generations of freedom fighters.Shah added that the slogan made Indians realise that self-rule was their right and not a favour bestowed by anyone.Describing Tilak as a fearless journalist, Shah said one could truly understand courage in journalism only by reading the articles published in Kesari, the newspaper founded by the freedom fighter."How fearless a journalist can be can only be experienced by reading the articles of Kesari," he said.Referring to Tilak's role in mobilising people through the public Ganesh and Shivaji festivals, Shah said they laid the foundation for cultural nationalism and that India continues to follow the path envisioned by the freedom fighter."India is now moving firmly on the path of cultural nationalism laid down by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and no one can reverse that journey," he said.Shah further added that Tilak's ideas on nationalism, self-rule and social awakening continue to guide the country and remain relevant for nation-building, particularly for the younger generation.Shah said honours such as the Lokmanya Tilak National Award are not merely ceremonial but recognise those who dedicate their lives to the country and inspire future generations."When such individuals are honoured, the feeling of gratitude of society towards them is discharged... Today, the Tilak Award that has been conferred upon Ajit Doval ji... for those who live for this country and work for this country, it will become a place of great inspiration," he said.Accepting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award, Doval thanked the organisers and said he was honoured to receive an award named after Lokmanya Tilak."I am thankful for this award named after Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and accept it with humility," Doval said.Doval also praised the country's leadership, saying, "We are very fortunate to have leaders like PM Modi and Amit Shah".
Article Summary: Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security. He said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him.
